name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately captures both responsibilities: it plays the on-screen death (flicker + decay/explosion) animation for dying party chars AND permanently marks them dead (flags |= 1). No address residue in the name; '2'/'4'-style suffixes absent.
purpose: Scan party slots for newly-dying chars (hp_current==0, flags bit0 not yet set), play their on-screen death flicker + decay/explosion animation, and permanently mark them dead.
logic_summary: Phase 1: iterate 0..data_fd2_battle_party_member_count-1; for each runtime char with flags bit0==0 AND hp_current==0 AND (pos_x,pos_y) inside the battle view window, cache its screen-pixel pointer (lgs + ((pos_y-1)-origin_y)*0x2AC0 + ((pos_x-1)-origin_x)*0x18 + 0x75D8) into stack array dying_screen_pos[] and count n_dying. If n_dying==0: set flags|=1 on every hp_current==0 char and return (silent off-screen death). Phase 2 (13-frame flicker, f=0..12): composite battle tile map into lgs+0x8088; for each non-dead char, if hp_current==0 set sprite_state[1]=f%4 then paint sprite; paint shadow overlay; blit_rectangle to mode13h; wait 1 BIOS tick. After loop set flags|=1 on every hp_current==0 char (PERMANENTLY DEAD). Phase 3 (decay/explosion, 12 frames split 0..5 + 6..11): malloc 0x25680 scratch buffer, composite a clean tile map into it, swap data_fd2_large_game_state_buffer_ptr to the scratch buffer, composite_all_chars_overlay, restore the pointer; fire death SFX via fd2_play_sfx_with_handle(...,3,1). Frames 0..5: blit per-frame death sprite (sheet base + *(sheet+(f+0x44)*4+6)) at each cached pos, no per-frame restore; frames 6..11: memmove the clean scratch back into the live buffer each frame first, then blit the death sprite. free(scratch); fd2_composite_battle_frame(0) final cleanup.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects: marks dying chars permanently dead (flags|=1) and renders the death animation to the mode13h primary.

notes: Source comment block (anicombt.c lines 400-436) is already thorough, accurate, and ASCII-only; it correctly matches the decompilation (off-screen silent-death path, the -1 on both pos axes, Phase 2 13-frame flicker, Phase 3 split 0..5/6..11 with memmove restore, death SFX with handle id 3).
